title: Constant-factor welfare from posted item prices
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Is there a universal α>0 such that every independent prior over subadditive buyers admits fixed anonymous item prices achieving expected welfare at least α E[OPT] for every fixed arrival permutation?
definitions: There are m distinct indivisible items M=[m] and n buyers. A valuation v:2^M→R_≥0 is normalized by v(∅)=0, monotone under set inclusion, and subadditive: v(S∪T)≤v(S)+v(T) for all S,T⊆M. A feasible allocation gives pairwise disjoint item subsets S_i to the buyers; unsold items are allowed. Welfare is ∑_i v_i(S_i), and OPT(v) is its maximum over feasible allocations. Each buyer’s valuation is drawn independently from a known Borel probability law on the finite-dimensional valuation space. Assume 0<E[OPT]<∞; zero-optimum instances are trivial. Prices p_j≥0 are finite reals chosen deterministically from the priors before values are drawn, and are the same for all buyers and throughout the process. For any fixed permutation of buyers, each arriving buyer knows its own full valuation, sees the remaining items R and purchases a subset S⊆R maximizing v_i(S)−∑_{j∈S}p_j. Items bought are removed. The guarantee must hold for every measurable choice among tied utility-maximizing bundles, even history-dependent choices. Welfare excludes payments. The same prices must work for all fixed permutations; the order cannot depend on realized valuations. There is no computation or demand-oracle bound on finding the prices or choosing a utility-maximizing bundle.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the proposition or its negation for the stated model. A positive answer must use one constant independent of n,m and the priors. A logarithmic or iterated-logarithmic loss, or prices depending on realized valuations, does not qualify.
context: The partitioning-valuation framework interpolates between subadditive and fractionally subadditive domains and describes posted-price guarantees that still depend on item count in the general subadditive case.
why: This asks whether a simple posted-price interface can match the welfare power of richer allocation mechanisms.

import_provenance.original_title: Constant-factor welfare from posted item prices
import_provenance.original_statement: For independent buyers with subadditive valuations over m items, do fixed anonymous item prices chosen from the known value distributions guarantee a universal constant fraction of expected optimal welfare, regardless of arrival order? This asks for posted prices specifically, beyond the known O(log log m) approximation.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Constant-factor combinatorial prophet inequalities using more general allocation rules do not settle this posted-price question.

sentences: Buyers have independent, known distributions over subadditive valuations.
The seller fixes one nonnegative price per item before seeing values.
Every buyer takes a utility-maximizing bundle from the remaining items.
One set of prices must work for all fixed arrival permutations and tie choices.
The goal is a constant expected fraction of optimal welfare.
